newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ cmmtte wants rethink on NZ$94 mln govt building.
newsitem.headline: NZ cmmtte wants rethink on NZ$94 mln govt building.

text.p: A parliamentary committee on Thursday recommended Cabinet reconsider plans to build a $94 million ministerial building and investigate the feasibility of moving the Beehive in order to extend Parliament House.

The Government Administration committee, which had considered a 200,000 signature petition opposing the building, recommended the Beehive continue to be used by ministers but that legislation be considered to cap the number of ministers.
The main parliament building, Parliament House, was designed in 1911 to have two wings, but only one was completed.
The Beehive, a conical building now housing ministers, was designed in the 1960s and built on the land where the second wing would have been.
The committee recommended studying the feasibility of moving the Beehive onto the site for the new building, about 100 metres away from the Beehive's present position and completing Parliament House.
It recommended the government's response to its report be debated in parliament.

One of the fiercest critics of the entire process, property magnate Sir Robert Jones, said in a statement he saw no reason to save the Beehive on account of its universally recognised functional inadequacies and its "grotesquely kitsch bad taste".
He said a far better option would be to remove it altogether, making way for the extended original building, and dump its pre-cast concrete panels in Wellington harbour to create an artificial reef.
